study.notes: STUDY: single centre randomised trial at Nanjing First Hospital (NCT01648582), 25 patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on oral agents assigned to once weekly dulaglutide (11 cases 0.75 mg, 5 cases 1.5 mg, patients and physicians blinded to the dose, n 16) or daily titrated insulin glargine (n 9) for 52 weeks; primary endpoint glucose fluctuation by continuous glucose monitoring. dose_mg empty because the dulaglutide arm pools the two doses. Tables 1 and 2 print baseline and 52 week values per arm as mean plus or minus SD with a between arm t and p at each timepoint, so the rows are taken by route arm_change_imputed_r with correlation 0.5; rows whose 52 week value is printed as a median with interquartile range (triglycerides, ALT, AST, fasting insulin, lipase, pancreatic enzymes, microalbumin) cannot be used, and fasting C peptide and HOMA-IR have no 52 week row at all. TNF alpha and IL-6 are printed as a median in one arm and a mean in the other at each timepoint, so neither yields a contrast. pct_weight_change from the Table 1 weight row, 68.97 to 69.06 kg equals plus 0.1 percent (glargine 62.56 to 64.67 kg, plus 3.4 percent; no contrast printed). Funded by the Scientific and Technological Development Program of Jiangsu Province, no conflicts declared (industry_funded FALSE); rob_overall some_concerns | BIBLIOGRAPHIC CORRECTION 2026-10-19: Europe PMC record for doi 10.1155/2019/2682657 (pmid 31950036) is 'The Effects of Once-Weekly Dulaglutide and Insulin Glargine on Glucose Fluctuation in Poorly Oral-Antidiabetic Controlled Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus', Wang J, Li HQ, Xu XH, Kong XC, Sun R, Jing T, Ye L, Su XF, Ma JH, Biomed Res Int 2019. The title names the dulaglutide versus insulin glargine comparison of NCT01648582 that this extraction describes. Two fields were wrong: the first author was recorded as Shao and is corrected to Wang, and the journal was recorded as J Diabetes Res, which is the journal of the companion trial in spec 188, and is corrected to Biomed Res Int. Shao appears nowhere in the author list of either paper. The tracked extraction file keeps its original name, which encodes the superseded surname.

json.design: single centre randomised trial, once weekly dulaglutide 0.75 or 1.5 mg (dose blinded) versus daily titrated insulin glargine, 25 patients with type 2 diabetes, 52 weeks, primary endpoint glucose fluctuation by continuous glucose monitoring
json.reason: full text group (Europe PMC); seven inventory markers with baseline and 52 week mean and SD in both arms, taken by the imputed change route
other_markers: total amylase, pancreatic enzymes and lipase
microalbumin and the albumin to creatinine ratio

rob.justification: randomly assigned in a 16 to 9 split with no sequence generation or concealment described and baseline imbalances in haemoglobin, haematocrit and red cell count (all p below 0.05) in 25 patients (D1 some concerns); open comparison of a weekly injection with titrated basal insulin, blinded only to the dulaglutide dose (D2 some concerns); no account of withdrawals or of why fasting C peptide and HOMA-IR have no 52 week row (D3 some concerns); laboratory and device measured outcomes (D4 low); the inventory markers are secondary to a continuous glucose monitoring primary endpoint, and several are reported as medians at 52 weeks only (D5 some concerns)

doubts: the dulaglutide arm pools 0.75 mg (11 patients) and 1.5 mg (5 patients); dose_mg is empty
the fasting glucose row favours insulin glargine, which is expected for a titrated basal insulin comparator and is a reason the comparator restriction of amendment R1 matters for question Q2
TNF alpha and IL-6 are printed as a mean with SD in one arm and a median with interquartile range in the other at the same timepoint, which cannot be reconciled; recorded as reported without variance
pct_weight_change plus 0.1 percent is arithmetic from the printed kilogram means and is expected to be flagged by the numbers check
